Hello and welcome to Voat!

No, at this time there is no way to disable images that I am aware of. Sorry.
If you want I can write a small script for it ^^

If you want to disable the thumbnails and nothing more or less, this is all you need to run via javascript:

$('head').append('<style> .thumbnail{display: none !important} </style>');

To run this automatically, you will need to use the extension Tampermonkey (for google chrome) or Greasemonkey (for firefox). Add a new script with this:

// ==UserScript==
// @name Disable voat.co thumbnails
// @version 0.1
// @description this disables thumbnails for posts on voat.co
// @author Zaro38
// @include http://voat.co/*
// @include http://*.voat.co/*
// @include https://voat.co/*
// @include https://*.voat.co/*
// @grant none
// ==/UserScript==

$('head').append('<style> .thumbnail{display: none !important} </style>');

You can disable/enable it by clicking the extension icon (or the arrow next to it if you use greasemonkey) and then click "Disable voat.co thumbnails".

Concerned but hopeful.

Concerned about a degradation and loss of our culture. Voat was a place where respectful discussion was the norm, even in heated arguments it was rare to see anyone make personal attacks, and memes too did not flood the front page of /v/all. This wasn't due to moderation, but just because of the kind of people that were here, and the choices they made about how to conduct themselves. My experiences with FPH on reddit were not pleasant, and I'm considerably underweight. I don't approve of bigotry or shaming anyone, especially when I know that it is difficult to change habits, and attacking someone for it only makes it worse. I would never want to be subjected to the vitriol I saw on my few encounters with users from that subreddit, and i certainly wouldn't want anyone I care about to be subjected to it either. So if users of that subreddit are the bulk of the new influx of users, my fear is that they will bring that culture over here and it will wash away our pre-existing one.

Previous waves of reddit users, of which I am a part, came to voat because we saw something in it which was admirable. It wasn't full of reactionary and extremist behaviors. It was just a nice place where the people were chill and we share links about news and things with each other.

While I've been here, I've observed a slight increase in the opinion that SJW is utter evilness and freedom of speech should trump everything ever ever, especially in cases where people are posting borderline child porn or borderline calls for violence against spouses. Even so, discussion on these things has been fairly rational and civil, and only a few weird people are actually posting that kind of content.

I am concerned about people who are overweight feeling they cannot participate on voat for fear of being attacked or persecuted. Chances are those who disagree most strongly with reddit's foolish and hasty implementation of their "keep everyone safe" rule were some of the first to jump ship and come over here. These are exactly the sort of people who ruin nice things. Not those who oppose censorship, but those who oppose civility and responsibility for actions - including speech. Those too who simply panicked, did not take a minute to consider whether the admins may have been attempting to do a good thing without evil intentions, who were swept up in the wave of outrage and mob justice were likely a not-insubstantial part of this influx.

I imagine that some people will call me a dumb/evil SJW for expressing these concerns, and dismiss me for that.

However I am hopeful. I've seen other new visitors who say they came not because they were from FPH or really agree with it, but because they are tired of reddit's mismanagement, tired of rampant censorship - whether from admins or mods - and want to try someplace new. I hope that even if people came from FPH that they can agree to respect the culture and norms of Voat and try to do what they can to elevate the tone and quality of discussion through conscious choice. I hope too that those with unrealistic expectations for Voat administration are able to temper that with empathy for atko and puttitout. Voat is still in Alpha, and new ideas and experimentation are still on the table and being tried out, so if something happens that you don't like, try not to fall into despair - just express your opinions with courtesy or at least without some of the insanity we've seen being thrown at the reddit admins when they make mistakes.
